claim: Formulas live in a 'formulas:' section of the .base file, are referenced as formula.<name>, and produce computed properties usable in any view; example shows formatted_price: 'if(price, price.toFixed(2) + " dollars")'.
quote:
formulas:
  formatted_price: 'if(price, price.toFixed(2) + " dollars")'
  ppu: "(price / age).toFixed(2)"

claim: Built-in file.* properties available on every note include file.name, file.ext, file.path, file.folder, file.tags (list), file.ctime, file.mtime, file.size, file.links, and file.embeds; user properties are referenced as note.<name> or just <name>.
quote: file.name (String) File name; file.tags (List) All tags in file content and frontmatter; file.ctime (Date) Created time; file.mtime (Date) Modified time; file.links (List) All internal links in the note

claim: Bases supports arithmetic (+ - * / % ()), comparison (== != > < >= <=), and boolean (! && ||) operators; date arithmetic uses duration strings like date + "1M" or date - "2h".
quote: Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, %, (). Comparison: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=. Boolean: !, &&, ||. Date arithmetic uses duration strings: date + "1M" or date - "2h"

claim: Global functions include if(condition, trueResult, falseResult?), now(), today(), date(), duration(), link(), list(), file(), image(), icon(), max(), min(), number() — covering conditionals, dates, and value coercion.
quote: if() – Conditional logic: "if(condition, trueResult, falseResult?)"; now() – Current datetime; today() returns midnight today; duration() – Parses duration strings for date arithmetic

claim: Date values expose .year/.month/.day/.hour fields plus .format(), .relative() (e.g. '3 days ago'), and .date()/.time() methods; subtracting two dates yields a Duration that must be unwrapped via .days/.hours before arithmetic.
quote: Fields: date.year, date.month, date.day, date.hour ... format(formatString) – Uses Moment.js format: "YYYY-MM-DD"; relative() – Human-readable comparison: "3 days ago". Date Math Examples: now() + '1d'

claim: List values support .filter(expression), .map(expression), .reduce(expression, initialValue), .contains/.containsAll/.containsAny, .join(separator), .unique(), .sort(), .reverse() — enabling derived tags/link aggregations.
quote: filter(expression) – Keep elements where true: "[1,2,3,4].filter(value > 2)"; map(expression) – Transform elements: "[1,2,3].map(value + 1)"; reduce(expression, initialValue)

claim: File objects support relational helpers asLink(display?), hasLink(otherFile), hasTag(...values), hasProperty(name), inFolder(folderName) — letting formulas turn raw links into resolved navigable titles.
quote: asLink(display?) – Create clickable link; hasLink(otherFile), hasTag(...values) – Relationship checks; hasProperty(name) – Property existence; inFolder(folderName) – Folder containment check

claim: A Bases view can be saved as a standalone .base file or embedded inside a Markdown note via a code block, with both forms sharing the same Bases syntax.
quote: The views themselves are described by the Bases syntax, which can be saved as a `.base` file or embedded in code blocks within your Markdown files.

claim: Embedded bases use a ```base fenced code block inside a note, while standalone .base files are embedded with ![[Projects.base]] or ![[Projects.base#View Name]] — and embedding shifts the meaning of 'this' to the host note, which often breaks filters written assuming the base file itself.
quote: when that view is embedded in a Person note, `this` becomes the embedding file ... Embedding syntax: ![[Projects.base]] or ![[Projects.base#View Name]]

claim: Concrete useful formulas include overdue flag if(due && status != "Done" && due < today(), "Overdue", ""), days-until-due ((due - today()) / 86400000).round(), relative modified file.mtime.relative(), and group-key list(area).unique().sort().join(", ").
quote: Overdue flag: if(due && status != "Done" && due < today(), "Overdue", ""); Due in days: if(due, ((due - today()) / 86400000).round(), null); Updated relative: file.mtime.relative()

claim: Regex matching uses /pattern/.matches(value); link-shape validation is feasible via list(sources).map(value.toString().startsWith("[[") && value.toString().endsWith("]]")).contains(false); 'this' inside an embedded base resolves to the host note, not the row being evaluated.
quote: /ø \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/.matches(file.name) ... list(sources).map(value.toString().startsWith("[[") && value.toString().endsWith("]]")).contains(false) ... the `this` variable, which references the currently selected note

claim: Bases re-renders reliably when frontmatter is edited through Obsidian's own properties UI, but plugins that write via app.vault.modify() can leave the metadata index stale until the cache is rebuilt (Settings → Files and Links → Rebuild Cache); using app.fileManager.processFrontMatter() avoids the issue.
quote: This plugin automatically updates a frontmatter status in a file. This is being updated within the file, but both Bases AND Dataview are not updating to reflect the change ... after that it will not update again until the cache is rebuilt.
